vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: prompt-crafter
Version: 3.0.1

The 'prompt-crafter' skill is an educational resource providing frameworks and templates for prompt engineering (RACE, Chain-of-Thought, etc.). The files (SKILL.md and references/frameworks.md) contain no executable code, network requests, or instructions that would lead to data exfiltration or system compromise; they are purely informational and align with the stated purpose.

llm.summary: The skill's requests and instructions align with its stated purpose (teaching how to craft prompts); it is an instruction-only skill with no installs, credentials, or surprising requirements.

dimensions.detail: Name/description promise (prompt engineering frameworks, examples, troubleshooting) matches the SKILL.md and reference examples. No binaries, env vars, or install steps are requested — consistent with an instruction-only prompt-crafting guide.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md stays within prompt-engineering guidance and includes frameworks, examples, and safety advice (refusal paths, testing adversarial inputs). It does include and discuss adversarial/jailbreak patterns (e.g., 'ignore all previous instructions') as something to test — this is expected for the topic but is a potential source of model-jailbreak vectors if reused carelessly.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files — the lowest-risk class (instruction-only). Nothing will be written to disk or auto-installed.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables, credentials, or config paths. That is proportionate for a prompt-authoring guide.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Skill is not always-enabled and uses default autonomous invocation settings. It does not request persistent system privileges or modify other skills' configurations.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is coherent with its stated purpose and doesn't request credentials or install code. Before installing: (1) remember the guide intentionally discusses jailbreak patterns — do not paste secrets or private data into prompts that include adversarial examples; (2) test examples in a safe environment (no real user data) since some suggested tests include 'ignore previous instructions' which can cause models to bypass intended safeguards; (3) note the source is 'unknown' (claims to be from an AI named Forge) — if provenance matters, ask the publisher for verification or prefer skills with a known homepage/owner; (4) follow the skill's own advice to include refusal paths and not to fabricate outputs when using its templates.
llm.findings: [ignore-previous-instructions] expected: The SKILL.md explicitly discusses adversarial inputs and gives 'ignore all previous instructions' as an example of what to test — this triggers the prompt-injection pattern detector but is contextually expected for a prompt-engineering guide rather than evidence of exfiltration or covert behavior.
